tasks.question: Where are the test tag identifiers processed and transformed during behave test execution in CEKit's testing framework?
tasks.reference_answer: Generator.get_tags returns name:version and name:latest (cekit/generator/base.py:134-136). BehaveTester.run selects the first or @wip (behave_tester.py:57-61). With no name filters, BehaveTestRunner.run computes a colon-stripped test_tag and uses @namespace,@full-name for slash-containing tags; otherwise it appends the original tag, retaining any version (behave_runner.py:44-57).

tasks.question: How does cekit's package management system handle package manager selection and validation across different container base images and build environments?
tasks.reference_answer: The package schema restricts manager to yum, dnf, or microdnf (cekit/descriptor/packages.py:23). Image.process_defaults assigns yum when packages.manager is absent (cekit/descriptor/image.py:80-82). This is a fixed fallback, not detection of the base image package manager; users must select a suitable supported manager.

tasks.question: Why does CEKit's package management system conditionally clear package manager metadata only when packages are installed rather than implementing a universal cache invalidation strategy?
tasks.reference_answer: The Dockerfile template emits package cleanup only when helper.packages_to_install(image) is truthy (cekit/templates/template.jinja:138-141). The cleanup macro calls the selected supported manager clean all and removes /var/cache/yum (25-29). Thus no cleanup RUN is generated when no packages are to be installed. Avoiding an unnecessary command is a consequence; the code alone does not prove historical rationale or performance gains.

tasks.question: Why does CEKit's test collection system require explicit tagging for behave test execution instead of running all collected tests by default?
tasks.reference_answer: CEKit collects shared steps, repository-root tests, module tests, and image tests (cekit/test/collector.py:53-72). BehaveTester defaults to the primary image tag or @wip (behave_tester.py:57-61), and BehaveTestRunner translates tags to selection arguments (behave_runner.py:49-57), which limits the combined suite. However, supplied test_names use --name instead of the tag loop (44-48). ~ignore is always supplied, while ~ci is added only in the tag branch when the user is not jenkins (37-64).

tasks.question: What is the architecture of timeout management across different builder implementations in cekit's container build system?
tasks.reference_answer: DockerBuilder reads positive integer DOCKER_TIMEOUT, default 600, as the daemon connection timeout (cekit/builders/docker_builder.py:51-62). OSBS _wait_for_osbs_task has timeout=7200 as a method default and checks current_time > timeout while polling every 20 seconds (cekit/builders/osbs.py:182-192,213-215). Buildah and Podman call subprocess.check_call(cmd) with no explicit timeout (buildah.py:52-53; podman.py:52-53). These govern different stages, not uniform maximum build durations.
